name: every-pass-along-the-dot-bar-magnifies-a-dot
description:
The magnification worked on some passes and not others. placeDotBloom appends a .dotbloom div to the same bar the pick walked, the bloom carries no .d glyph, and a pick that landed on it threw inside paint - which left the held index on the bloom, so every following pass early-returned and the bar stayed dead until the cursor left. The unit suite can build that shape by hand, but only the running product says whether the bloom is really a sibling of the dots. This puts the pointer on alternating dots ten times and counts how many passes actually wore the chip, then does it once more after a space switch has rebuilt the bar.

THE BLOOM IS ASSERTED PRESENT FIRST. Without it the ten passes below run against a bar that never had the trap in it, and would pass on the broken code too.

ALTERNATING DOTS, NOT A SWEEP. paint returns early when the pick has not changed, so ten moves along one dot would count one magnification and nine no-ops. Moving between two dots makes every pass a real repaint, and the centre of the other dot is far enough for the hysteresis to release the held pick.

actions.expression: (() => { const bar = document.querySelector('.spacedots'); if (!bar) return 'no-bar'; const bloom = bar.querySelector('.dotscroll > .dotbloom'); return bloom ? 'bloom-is-a-sibling' : 'no-bloom'; })()
actions.note: the trap itself: a child of the bar that is not a dot

actions.expression: (() => { const bar = document.querySelector('.spacedots'); if (!bar) return 'no-bar'; const dots = [...bar.querySelectorAll('.sdot')]; if (dots.length < 2) return 'dots ' + dots.length; let landed = 0; for (let i = 0; i < 10; i++) { const target = dots[i % 2]; const box = target.getBoundingClientRect(); bar.dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('mousemove', {bubbles: true, clientX: box.left + box.width / 2, clientY: box.top + box.height / 2})); if (bar.querySelector('.sdot.mag') === target) { landed++; } } return String(landed); })()
actions.note: THE MEASUREMENT: how many of ten consecutive passes put the chip on the dot under the cursor

actions.expression: (() => { const bar = document.querySelector('.spacedots'); bar.dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('mouseleave', {bubbles: true})); return String(bar.querySelectorAll('.sdot.mag').length); })()

actions.note: a space switch rebuilds the dots bar, so the pass below meets fresh elements

actions.expression: (() => { const bar = document.querySelector('.spacedots'); if (!bar) return 'no-bar'; const target = bar.querySelector('.sdot'); if (!target) return 'no-dot'; const box = target.getBoundingClientRect(); bar.dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('mousemove', {bubbles: true, clientX: box.left + box.width / 2, clientY: box.top + box.height / 2})); const chip = bar.querySelector('.sdot.mag'); return chip === target ? 'chip' : 'no-chip'; })()
actions.note: A rebuilt bar has to answer a cursor move the same way the first one did
one chip, not two: a throw mid-paint leaves the previous dot still wearing .mag

assertions.desc: setup: the bloom really is a child of the bar, so the ten passes below meet the trap
Every one of ten consecutive passes magnified the dot under the cursor
the bar settles back, so the rebuild pass starts from nothing
A magnification after a sidebar rebuild behaves like one after a plain move
exactly one chip: a throw inside paint would leave the previous dot marked too

assertions.label: no-throw-in-the-pick
assertions.desc: the wedge announced itself as a TypeError on every pass
